top_cited_works.title: An Arduino-Based RFID Platform for Animal Research
top_cited_works.abstract: Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) technology has been broadly applied in the biological sciences to yield new insights into behavior, cognition, population biology, and distributions. RFID systems entail wireless communication between small tags that, when stimulated by an appropriate radio frequency transmission, emit a weak, short-range wireless signal that conveys a unique ID number. These tags, which often operate without a battery, can be attached to animals such that their presence at a particular location can be detected by an RFID reader. This paper describes an RFID data-logging system that can serve as the core for a wide variety of field and laboratory applications for monitoring the activities of individual animals. The core electronics are modeled on an Arduino circuit board, which is a hobbyist electronics system. Users can customize the hardware and software to accommodate their needs. We demonstrate the utility of the system with cursory descriptions of three real-world research applications. The first is a large-scale deployment that was used to examine individual breeding behaviors across four local populations of Wood Ducks. The second application employed...

top_cited_works.title: Limitations and mechanisms influencing the migratory performance of soaring birds
top_cited_works.abstract: Migration is costly in terms of time, energy and safety. Optimal migration theory suggests that individual migratory birds will choose between these three costs depending on their motivation and available resources. To test hypotheses about use of migratory strategies by large soaring birds, we used GPS telemetry to track 18 adult, 13 sub‐adult and 15 juvenile Golden EaglesAquila chrysaetosin eastern North America. Each age‐class had potentially different motivations during migration. During spring, the migratory performance (defined here as the directness of migratory flight) of adults was higher than that of any other age‐classes. Adults also departed earlier and spent less time migrating. Together, these patterns suggest that adults were primarily time‐limited and the other two age‐classes were energy‐limited. However, adults that migrated the longest distances during spring also appeared to take advantage of energy‐conservation strategies such as decreasing their compensation for wind drift. During autumn, birds of all age‐classes were primarily energy‐minimizers; they increased the length of stopovers, flew less direct routes and migrated at a slower pace than during spring...

recent_works.title: Defining Requirements for Safe, Scalable, and Seamless Surface Navigation for UAS: Challenges and Perspectives
recent_works.abstract: The main obstacle to autonomous navigation operations for large UAS in civil airspace is the lack of safe and reliable automatic taxiing, takeoff, and landing. The SurfNav4UAS project aims at addressing the challenges of automatic taxiing, with a specific focus on developing safe, scalable, and seamless navigation methods that meet the unique accuracy, integrity, and continuity requirements of automatic surface operations. This work outlines the methodology for defining navigation requirements.

recent_works.title: Fourier Series Quadratic Bézier Approximation for Gradient Vector Field Trajectory Following
recent_works.abstract: This work investigated precise arrival-time control for uncrewed aerial vehicles with turnrate– constrained dynamics. Trajectory planning and following with Bézier curves allowed for time-controlled interceptions by providing continuous curved paths that meet arrival time requirements and did not violate fixed-wing aircraft turning constraints. Bézier curves were parametric and required approximation of original routes for Gradient Vector Field (GVF)-based trajectory following to overcome the discretization problem inherent in waypointbased tracking. The specific problem of this work was identifying a length and arrival time controllable trajectory function that was partially differentiable using Fourier series as a curve fitting basis function. Arrival time deviations and tracking error experiments were conducted in two-dimensional kinematic airplane simulations using GVF tracking and the non-linear guidance law for comparison. Fourier series routes for convergence towards the route resulted in improved path tracking and arrival time adhesion when compared to the NGL and polynomial regression approximation of the Bézier route.

recent_works.title: Integrity Aware Hybrid Camera LiDAR Trilateration
recent_works.abstract: Safe autonomous aircraft operation benefits from continuous position estimates when GNSS signals are degraded or unavailable due to buildings, foliage, jamming, or interference. Hybrid camera–LiDAR localization is a supplemental localization solution that uses visual recognition to identify signs or other distinct landmarks, estimates ranges using LiDAR, and computes receiver position using trilateration, but currently lacks a direct measure of integrity. Receiver Autonomous Integrity Monitoring (RAIM) is a standard technique for measuring the integrity of a GNSS solution for aircraft, but it considers ranging variances for each satellite or landmark to be equal. Instead,Weighted-RAIM (WRAIM) weighted specific trust in landmark ranges based on the quality of a surface fit provided by Random Sample Consensus (RANSAC) surface fitting to extract landmark-specific variances. Indoor experiments were conducted in a Vicon motion capture environment to identify the impact of WRAIM on the integrity of hybrid camera–LiDAR localization. recent_works.title: Perpendicular Scenario Collision Avoidance With Quadratic Bézier Curve Trajectory Planning
recent_works.abstract: Congested airspace conflict resolution during terminal operations can be fatal if air traffic controllers and pilots are not well-coordinated. Aircraft that receive takeoff or landing clearance at inappropriate times, whether at vertiports or traditional airports, risk colliding with descending traffic before pilots can react. In a high-density airspace, coordination between air traffic controllers and aircraft (crewed or uncrewed) becomes significantly more challenging than in current commercial operations, rendering traditional conflict resolution methods potentially infeasible. The complexity further increases at vertiports, where aircraft can arrive and depart from any direction. Relying solely on air traffic controllers to relay collision avoidance information in such environments may not be practical. The presented work investigated a generic method of automated collision avoidance during terminal operations, specifically in scenarios where one aircraft cannot see the other and vertical maneuvers are not feasible, due to already occurring altitude changes. recent_works.title: Approach Pattern Automation With Quadratic Bézier Curve Trajectory Planning
recent_works.abstract: Current procedures for sequencing and scheduling arriving aircraft are designed to handle 2-3 aircraft at a time and rely heavily on communication between air traffic controllers and pilots. However adherence to a First Come First Served (FCFS) order, along with the use of holding patterns or go-arounds, may lead to inefficient energy usage and unnecessary delays. Scaling the Federal Aviation Administration’s current scheduling methods to a high-density, semi-autonomous airspace, such as Advanced Air Mobility, presents possible challenges in terms of controller workload, aircraft sequencing, and cascading delays. Scheduling challenges become even more pronounced at vertiports, where aircraft can approach and land from any direction. The presented work investigates trajectory planning techniques that ensure multiple aircraft can make coordinated arrival path interceptions while adhering to assigned sequences and Scheduled Times of Arrival (STAs).
